faq.q: Why does ice float on a lake?
faq.a: When water freezes, its molecules lock into an open pattern that takes more space, so ice is less dense than liquid water and floats.
asks: Why does ice stay on top?

faq.q: Why is the bottom of a frozen lake 4 °C?
faq.a: Fresh water is densest at about 4 degrees Celsius. Water at that temperature sinks to the bottom, while colder, lighter water stays above it.
asks: Why is the deep water warmer in winter?

faq.q: How do fish survive under ice?
faq.a: The water below the ice stays liquid at around 4 degrees. Fish slow down in the cold and live there until spring.
asks: Where do fish go in winter?

faq.q: Why does ice insulate the water below?
faq.a: Ice, and especially snow on top of it, conduct heat poorly, so they slow the loss of heat from the water to the freezing air.
asks: Does ice keep the lake warm?

faq.a: Shallow ponds can freeze right to the bottom in very cold places, but deep lakes almost never do, thanks to the ice lid and the 4 degree water.
asks: Can a pond freeze all the way down?

facts: Fresh water is densest at about 4 degrees Celsius.
